findings.claim: MaximumObjectGraphDepth for UntrustedData is changed from 500 to 5000. This is unrelated to the requirement and weakens a security limit (ledger L9 records a stack depth limit of 500). No test in the diff covers it.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test that deserializes a 501-deep nested structure with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData and expects MessagePackSerializationException/InsufficientExecutionStackException. It passes on base and fails on head. Alternatively, run a mutation on line 38 (5000 -> 500) and see whether any test in the diff fails.

findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper in the constructor has no negative test. Nothing asserts that diagnostics for in-compilation types still get reported, or that metadata-located ones are dropped. The new tests only use VerifyCS with no expected diagnostics. If the guard were removed or negated to suppress everything, the tests would still pass, since they only assert that no diagnostics exist.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:239 negate-condition: `diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && ContainsSyntaxTree` -> `false` (drop all analyzer diagnostics); expected to survive because every new test expects zero diagnostics, and the existing MsgPack00x analyzer tests may be the only thing that would catch it.

findings.claim: The GetPropertyIdentifierLocation change (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull) is not exercised. Neither new metadata test has a property with a null key that reaches this line. The `ClosedGenericRecordStruct` test uses a keyed property. The null-location behaviour is not tested.

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector.cs:985 delete-statement: revert to `item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` indexing; expected to survive if the tests do not reach the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path with a metadata symbol.

findings.claim: The MemberNeedsKey change from `[0]` to `FirstOrDefault()?` is covered only by the unkeyed-member test, whose MyGenericStruct is defined in a referenced assembly. A mutant that reverts to `[0]` might be killed there, but the ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter drops the diagnostic anyway. The null-location guard on its own is therefore redundant and untested.

The tests set TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck, so the generated output is not verified in the analyzer run. The generator check in the helper only asserts that a hint name exists, not that the resolver contains a formatter for the closed generic. The MyGenericStruct<int> formatter case could be wrong or missing without any test noticing.

receipt_plan.detail: Mutate the generator so the resolver is emitted without a formatter for the closed generic struct; the tests still pass because only the hint name is checked.

questions.text: Is the MaximumObjectGraphDepth change from 500 to 5000 in UntrustedData intentional and in scope?
options: Intentional, a separate deliberate security decision
questions.why_it_matters: Per L9, a depth of 500 is a deliberate security limit. If accidental, this is a high-severity regression to revert. If intentional, it still needs its own test and rationale.
